editorial:
Imagine being a prisoner in the US and getting a deal you cannot refuse: go on a dangerous mission into Vietnam to blow up some old missiles, and you get your freedom. That is exactly what happens to a ragtag group of Chinese fighters in this wild ride. It feels like a mix between a war movie and a classic kung fu flick. The chemistry between the teammates is great, and you can tell they are just trying to survive while dealing with a mission that seems almost impossible. It has a gritty but fun energy that keeps you glued to the screen.

What really makes this one a winner is the action. Sammo Hung knows how to choreograph fights, and the stunts are totally crazy. The pacing is fast, though some of the dialogue can feel a bit dated. If you love old-school martial arts and explosions, you need to see this. For the best experience, try to find the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection so you can see every punch clearly. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a solid way to check it out without spending too much.
endingExplained: In the final act, the team manages to find the missile depot and set the explosives. However, they have to fight through waves of enemies to get out alive. After a massive battle, the remaining survivors successfully blow up the base. They barely escape the blast zone and finally get the pardons they were promised. It ends on a high note with the survivors celebrating their freedom after surviving a suicide mission.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s action and kung fu movies.
